segments: 430. From the Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
King Leon.
And in this year, not only from the Franks of the region of the West did fear fall upon the Arabs,
but also and especially from the Tatars, who burst forth and came out from the East,
and reached as far as Hamadan, Azerbaijan, Arran, and Arzan {OCR?}, and wrought bitter disasters throughout all Persia.
And in this same year 617 [1220/1221],
in the third Arab month,
died al-Malik al-Qahir 'Izz al-Din Mas'ud, son of Nur al-Din, the lord of Mosul,
after reigning seven years and nine months.
For this man continually feared death,
and hastened to indulge himself,
as one who was snatching his pleasures from the hands of death.
And in his place reigned Nur al-Din Arslan Shah, his eldest son,
a youth of ten (twenty) years, who had been named after his elder brother.
And when al-Malik al-Qahir died,
he appointed Badr al-Din Lu'lu' as guardian of his son,
just as he had been his own administrator.
And that Badr al-Din acted admirably,
and sent to the caliph al-Nasir,
and brought a royal diploma (sigillion) for the youth.
And likewise he sent to the rest of the kings,
and confirmed the peace.
And he took possession of the kingdom of Mosul without disturbance,
even though there were many who sought the youth's life and were eager to reign:
'Imad al-Din, his uncle, the lord of 'Aqr,
and his father's uncles.
And Badr al-Din restrained them all by his conduct.
And he multiplied benefits to the magnates and the leaders among the sons of the city and the territory,
and they all loved him.
Now 'Imad al-Din, the lord of 'Aqr, the uncle of the youth,
sent to Muzaffar al-Din Gökböri, son of Zayn al-Din, the lord of Erbil, and said to him:
"Badr al-Din intends to act deceitfully against our house,
and to take the kingdom for himself."
Then Muzaffar al-Din helped the lord of 'Aqr,
and went and took the fortress of 'Imadiyya.
And Badr al-Din gathered forces and went against 'Imadiyya
to wage war against it
and capture 'Imad al-Din.
And because it was wintertime,
and there was much snow in those mountains,
Badr al-Din left off and returned to Mosul.
And 'Imad al-Din was strengthened,
and sent to the rest of the fortresses of the Hakkari and Zawzan regions,
and gained dominion over them.
